newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric front months end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric front months end slightly higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures front months ended slightly higher in lackluster trade that suffered from a lack of influencial news, industry sources said.

March California Oregon Border (COB) settled up two cents at $10.32 after trade in a range of $10.25-10.35, while April COB ended down five cents at $9.85 from trade in a range of $9.75-9.90 per megawatt hour (MWh).
August and September COB each ended down five cents at $17.50 and $17.55 per MWh respectively.
March Palo Verde (PV) finished up five cents at $13.30 from trading as low as $13.15, while April PV was untraded.
June and July PV ended down five and 15 cents at $15.35 and $20.45 per MWh respectively.
"The only piece of news that the market is still digesting is the hydro situation in the West," one Houston-based futures trader said, noting little other news was having an influence on the market.
Forecasts have called for much above normal spring water runoff levels to boost hydroelectric generation in the West into the summer months.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 117 COB and 66 PV contracts traded Wednesday.
